this condition should be in the connector, and probably be more like `typeof helper.state.relevancyStrictness !== 'undefined'`, wdyt?

If it's `0`, it's not smartly sorted. There are two cases when we get `0` as `relevancyStrictness`

1. customers set it like that on dashboard (meaning they don't want smart sort on the index)
2. a user clicked "see all results" button from <SmartSort /> and InstantSearch attached `relevancyStrictness=0` to the search parameter to suppress the smart setting (even it was configured on dashboard).

Does it make sense?

body: I don't really know how the templates work, but I think we should handle the case where `nbHits === nbSortedHits`, to avoid this kind of sentences `10,000 relevant results sorted out of 10,000 found in 1ms`
yes, that's an important note! isSmartSorted should be false in that case IMO

I just handled it [like that](https://github.com/algolia/react-instantsearch/pull/3010/files#diff-7f595657982de401bfc86c6843f6e39d019e23ae53ff282e017303121a455a1bR63) in RIS, should I fix it before merging `smartSort`?
I think so, but @eunjae-lee and you have been closer to the implementation of this feature, wdyt?
If we think `isSmartSorted` reflect what the engine says, it should stay like that. But it make sense to consider that if the number of results are the same we consider it has `not smart sorted`. 🤔
Added here: https://github.com/algolia/react-instantsearch/pull/3009/commits/9fa94a9e4274839ae05026581a57d3611a323365, wdyt @eunjae-lee ?

I think `isSmartSorted` should stay as is. With `0 < appliedRelevancyStrictness`, it's indeed smartly sorted from the engine. It's just the result happen to be the same as normal sort. Giving another meaning to `isSmartSort` could be confusing (like "why is it false? I set the value on dashboard?")

However it'd be a good addition in detail to render proper text. So I'm thinking of the change only in stats. What do you think? @Haroenv @shortcuts

> Giving another meaning to isSmartSort could be confusing (like "why is it false? I set the value on dashboard?")

It could be confusing from a developer POV indeed, but I think it make sense to consider that if the hits are the same as the sorted hits, then it's not smart sorted. As the boolean isn't `isSmartSortConfigured` for example, we can take this liberty IMO

When it's configured but happens to have the same number of hits, if we follow your logic, we should display a button saying "See relevant results" because isSmartSort === false. And when clicking the button will `refine(undefined)`, which will do nothing (because it's already undefined). That's confusing, no?
True, this would add a lot of conditions to handle it!
Should we disable the button on the default template when the hits are matching then? Or do we let the user handle this case? (for IS, as RIS doesn't provide a default template)

It will likely happen when there's empty query, etc. IMO we can release the smartSort widget as-is, and update only the default template in stats widget. If we get better understanding and learn patterns, we could add some logic to smartSort, but I feel it's too early to assume conditional behaviors.
Ok, I'll revert it to [`nbHits !== nbSortedHits`](https://github.com/algolia/react-instantsearch/pull/3010/files#diff-7f595657982de401bfc86c6843f6e39d019e23ae53ff282e017303121a455a1bR63) then!
but let's hear what @Haroenv thinks

I disagree, empty query for example looks very odd now on a smart sort, and should be handled as a non-smart sort.

Similarly for example if you search for an item with "paginationLimitedTo" hits, today this will give "paginationLimited to out of nbHits", but that's an engine bug, and should be "nbHits out of nbHits", which will act as if it's not smart sorted (no need to unsort it if the results will be the same).

cc @Ant-hem, what do you think?

@Haroenv not sure if I understand you correctly.
My suggestion was

**With appliedRelevancyStrictness > 0, when nbSortedHits === nbHits:**
1. Display the stat as `1000 hits in 10ms` (without smart sort mentioned)
2. Display the button as `See all results` (still as if it's a smart sort)

Which part do you disagree? Do you think we should display the button as `See relevant results` or not display the button at all?

Chiming there! I don't have a *strong opinion* on that topic but I can help by giving you some context and pointers on the feature.

The idea behind the banner was to be "transparent" with the end-users as the algorithm can be perceived as a "black-box". That's why I am not really disturbed by the following:

> `10,000 relevant results sorted out of 10,000 found in 1ms`

That's just means all the available hits were selected and then sorted by the Algorithm. I don't see anything weird with it, just the "transparency" we initially wanted.

On top on that, relying on `nbHits` can be dangerous as this value can sometimes, be interpolated by the engine and thus being volatile/an approximation. See `exhaustiveNbHits` field in the response.

To finish, one rule of thumb is `relevancyStrictness=0` means that the algorithm is disabled and that no results selection/deletion is being done. It's *almost* (not exactly) equivalent to a hard sort. When `relevancyStrictness> 0`  the algorithm is enabled and it does select/remove results.

Hope that helps!

I think the button should be displayed, so for the context of SmartSort, isSmartSorted is true as long as appliedRelevancyStrictness is not 0, but in the stats widget I think it doesn't make sense to show "x relevant results shown out of x in yms", but it should be "x results found in yms", which correlates with isSmartSorted: false
